pages.x: In 602 a rough centurion named Phocas led a mutiny, seized the throne in Constantinople and had the emperor Maurice and his sons put to death. The Persian king, Khosrow II, owed his throne to Maurice, who had helped him win it back years before, and he declared war to avenge him.

Khosrow's armies took the great frontier fortress of Dara in 604, then overran Roman Mesopotamia and Armenia. In 610 Heraclius, son of the governor of Africa, sailed from Carthage, overthrew Phocas and became emperor, but he inherited an eastern front in collapse.

In 614 the Persians took Jerusalem after a short siege. Thousands of its people were killed, churches were burned, and the True Cross, believed to be the cross of Christ, was carried off to the Persian capital, Ctesiphon. By 619 they had taken Egypt too, the granary that fed Constantinople.

Heraclius made peace with the Avars, melted down church treasure to pay his troops, and in 622 crossed to Asia Minor to train a new army. In 624 he marched into the heart of Persia and destroyed its holiest fire temple, at Ganzak. For three years he outfought one Persian army after another.

In 626 Khosrow struck at the capital itself. A Persian army camped across the Bosporus while a vast horde of Avars and Slavs attacked the land walls, and Heraclius stayed in the east. The defenders sank the Slavs' canoes as they tried to ferry the Persians across, and the Avars gave up. The city thanked the Virgin Mary.

With the Western Turks pouring into the Caucasus as his allies, Heraclius invaded Mesopotamia, and in December 627 destroyed a Persian army near the ruins of Nineveh, killing its general, it is said, in single combat. He sacked Khosrow's palace at Dastagird and marched on Ctesiphon.

Khosrow was overthrown and killed by his own son in February 628, and the new king made peace, handing back all the lands Persia had taken. In 630 Heraclius carried the True Cross back into Jerusalem in triumph.

After 26 years of war the frontier was back where it had been, and both empires were bled white. Within a decade the armies of a new faith, Islam, burst out of Arabia. They took Syria, Jerusalem and Egypt from the Romans, and swept the Persian empire away altogether.
pts: Both empires were left open to the Arabs
